summary.headline: JK Cement Q2 FY27 net sales rose 21% YoY to INR3,561 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR500 crore on fuel-cost pressure; H1 volume up 19% to 11.3 MT.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 net sales grew 21% YoY to INR3,561 crore, driven by grey cement volume growth, though down 9% QoQ. Quarterly EBITDA was INR500 crore versus INR440 crore a year ago and INR639 crore in Q1, with the company attributing the QoQ fall to rising fuel costs and only partial pass-through. Management guided to FY27 grey volume of 23 MT or more and flagged a fuel cost step-up in Q3 and Q4 (Kcal cost possibly toward INR2 from INR1.71), partly offset by a price hike of about INR20 per bag from mid-September. Net debt rose to INR4,571 crore, with net debt/EBITDA of 1.95x, and management expects a peak near INR6,000 crore on the 50 MT plan.

segments.name: Grey cement
segments.commentary: H1 volume 11.3 MT, up 19%; growth led by Central India expansion (6 MT completed March 2026). Management says it held share in North and gained share in Central India.

segments.name: White cement and putty
segments.commentary: H1 volume 10.32 lakh tons, up 19%. Nathdwara wall putty plant (0.6 MT) commissioned, taking India white/putty capacity to 3.05 MT and total including UAE to 3.65 MT. Fujairah export constrained to GCC only.

segments.name: Paints (JK Maxx)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR116 crore; H1 about INR250 crore; FY27 guidance of INR500-550 crore maintained. Q2 EBITDA loss INR2 crore; management targets positive EBITDA for FY27 and 3-5% margin in FY28, with long-term target of 35-38%.

segments.name: RMC and construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR60 crore in Q2 (INR50 crore in Q1). 23 RMC plants operating, targeting 50 by March 2027; no EBITDA yet, with about 6 months per plant to breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 grey cement volume guidance of 23 MT or more; management says 24 MT is possible but not committed.
Fuel cost per Kcal at INR1.71 in Q2; could rise toward INR2, with about INR80-90 impact in Q3 and a similar amount in Q4. Power and fuel cost expected to rise INR80-100 per quarter.
Price increase of about INR20 per bag (trade and non-trade) from mid-September to October; management says another INR10-15 per bag is needed to cover costs.
Net debt/EBITDA may peak at 2.25-2.35x around end-FY27; net debt may peak near INR6,000 crore on the 50 MT plan; target below 1.5x from FY29.

Capex about INR3,500 crore in FY27, then about INR2,500 crore per year in the brownfield phase. Jaisalmer integrated plant expected in H1 FY28; Bikaner grinding H1 FY28; Bathinda targeted by September 2027.
Paint business: no further investment needed beyond INR130 crore approved (75,000 KL plant, INR600 crore paint limit); future investment to be self-funded.
capex_capacity: Nathdwara wall putty plant (0.6 MT) commissioned in H1 FY27.
Jaisalmer integrated site in advanced stage, on schedule for H1 FY28 commissioning.
Bikaner grinding station progressing; commissioning targeted H1 FY28.
Bathinda grinding station: approvals received (EC and CTE formal letters expected within October); target completion by September 2027.
Mahan coal block: work started; first-half FY29 operational target; coal cost expected INR1-1.25 per ton. Second block (West Shahdol) 6-8 months behind.
Post-FY28 brownfield expansion of about 11 MT at Muddapur and Panna (roughly 5-6 MT each). Bihar plant utilisation about 50% after 8 months.
Clinker utilisation 95% in Q2 after kiln maintenance; cement utilisation about 67-70%.
demand_pricing: Maharashtra and Karnataka mostly sold out; management sees no significant drought impact. South plants are about 15% of volume.
UP elections unlikely before March; Diwali and Delhi construction curbs are near-term risks to Q3 volumes.
Price up about INR20 per bag from mid-September to October; management says white cement prices are unlikely to rise further.
Fuel mix in Q2: Indian coal 55%, petcoke 30-35%, alternate fuels 13%. CC ratio 1.5.
Paint margin target 35-38% versus competitor margins above 40%; advertising is allocated across Max X brand for paint, putty and white cement.

qa_highlights.question: How should H2 volumes be viewed given drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra and UP elections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Karnataka and Maharashtra are mostly sold out, and no significant impact is expected. FY27 guidance is 23 MT or more, and 24 MT is possible if conditions hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of higher petcoke and domestic coal prices on cost per Kcal?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost could rise from INR1.71 toward INR2 per Kcal, with a partial impact in Q3 and the full impact in Q4, around INR80-90 per quarter each.

qa_highlights.question: Is the paint business justified as a standalone investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the business should reach positive EBITDA in FY27, with a 2-3% annual profitability improvement thereafter. The INR130 crore 75,000 KL paint plant was approved, taking total paint investment to the INR600 crore limit.

qa_highlights.question: Where will net debt peak and what capex is required?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is about INR4,571 crore and could peak near INR6,000 crore on the 50 MT plan. Net debt/EBITDA may reach 2.25-2.35x around end-FY27. Capex is about INR3,500 crore in FY27 and about INR2,500 crore per year after.

qa_highlights.question: How much further price increase is needed after Diwali?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR10-15 per bag more is needed to cover cost increases, including packaging (PP granules) and fuel. Price action could come after Diwali, when construction slows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone white cement volumes grow 13-14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says volumes previously served from Fujairah are now supplied from India, and market growth also contributed. Fujairah is limited to GCC exports.

risks_watch: Fuel cost step-up in Q3 and Q4 (Kcal cost toward INR2) with only partial price pass-through; INR10-15 per bag still uncovered.
Rupee weakness would raise granule and packaging costs, per management.
Peak net debt of about INR6,000 crore and net debt/EBITDA of 2.25-2.35x at end-FY27 during the 50 MT expansion.
Fujairah constraint on white cement exports and possible shortfall versus white cement growth guidance of 8-10%.
Paint EBITDA loss in Q2 and FY27 breakeven target; RMC still loss-making with a fixed tolling cost burden.
Bathinda approval timing and Jaisalmer/Bikaner commissioning in H1 FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and capacity timelines, but cautious on cost, noting Q3-Q4 fuel pressure and that further price increases in white cement are challenging. Evasive on segment-level profitability, declining to split grey and white EBITDA per ton.
